title: Jurisdictions: a state's record reviewed by the team (R8's note), the R17 gate fixed, Colorado's and Utah's records drafted
why: decisions/0164 R8's note (the attorney's review advised, not required) and the session manager's ruling on J1 (option b): the team (role 25) reviews a jurisdiction record, Jurisdictions::OPENED (AZ, NM) is kept until their records are reviewed, and CO and UT are written up as drafts whose laws say 'Found by search, not yet read against its official text'. HubOpening::lawSigned compared UPPER(code) with 'AZ' while records are keyed 'US-AZ', so R17's gate never matched: it now needs the US and the state record reviewed. tier() follows Q8: a sensitive place is story only off a nation's land, restricted on it. The reading rule is in code: a record can't be marked reviewed while any of its laws still reads "not yet read against its official text"; Mark read beside the law takes its official link and takes those words off (logged). Downstream of tier(), Landmarks::decide()/publiclyKnown() still hold a sensitive place no public source presents (no article, no visitor page) as held, whatever tier() returns, and anything on a nation's land stays held (tested). Tier 4 review: CEO, 2026-11-27, Prior Ruling Check yes (0164 R8 note, Q8; R17 repair). Tested: tools/jurisdiction-tests/j1.php, 31 checks on MariaDB.

changes.what: A jurisdiction record is marked reviewed by a person or a team role, the attorney's review optional with its date; Undo the review puts it back to draft; each review and undo is in the logbook
A law found by search shows Mark read with a box for its official text; Mark reviewed stays greyed with the reason until every law is read

Colorado and Utah appear as draft records with the laws found so far, each marked not yet read against its official text; New Mexico gains its unmarked-burials statute's citation. Nothing opens: drafts stay closed
A hub's opening (R17) waits for the US and its state record to be reviewed, and says so
FAQ: "Why isn't there a guide for my state yet?" says the team reviews a state's record (an attorney advised) and that Colorado's and Utah's are being written up

data_reason: The migration adds the column reviewed_as to jurisdictions (guarded, safe to run twice), inserts the US-CO and US-UT draft records (INSERT IGNORE) and their laws and New Mexico's burial statute only where they aren't there yet, and writes the notes of those two new draft records. No reviewed record is changed and nothing is deleted.
